guide_verdict: 2 stars, woody floral: pleasant but holds little interest
note: The Guide files it as a woody floral and does not mention the pineapple or the mossy base, so it neither confirms nor contradicts the fruity-chypre tags.

guide_verdict: 3 stars, fruity cola: a fruity, syrupy oriental, less grand than it claims

changes.reason: Scent and Chemistry says the Ambroxan core is sweetened with about 3% ethyl maltol (cooked sugar) and the Guide calls it syrupy, yet no stage carries the sugar family.
changes.quote: "sweetened by an outrageous amount of ca. 3% of ethyl maltol"

changes.reason: The ethyl maltol dose is described as a structural part of the main accord, so the sugar should persist beside the Ambroxan in the drydown.
changes.quote: "counterbalanced by an even more extreme amount of ethyl maltol"

changes.reason: The Guide's whole description is of a fruit-punch, syrupy smell, while the opening is tagged only saffron and jasmine.
changes.quote: "count on this oriental being a fruity, syrupy experience"

note: Scent and Chemistry also reports about 12% Evernyl, a synthetic oakmoss material, which would put oakmoss_chypre in the drydown on composition alone; not proposed because neither source describes a mossy smell.

guide_verdict: 2 stars, woody-amber amber: amber dominated by a harsh woody-amber material

changes.reason: The Guide says a very large dose of a woody-amber aromachemical dominates the scent, but the drydown tags it at 0.3 under resinous amber.
changes.quote: "a huge dose of some vile woody-amber material"

changes.reason: The Guide describes the woody-amber as loud enough to cover the rest of the composition, so it belongs in the heart as well.
changes.quote: "the kind that smells like rubbing alcohol played at heavy metal concert volume"

note: The pyramid lists only resinous amber, benzoin, tonka and vanilla; the Guide's category label names woody-amber first.

guide_verdict: 2 stars (EDT review), chocolate cucumber: the original accord now feels dated

changes.reason: The Guide names chocolate as the first element of Black Orchid's defining accord, but no stage carries the cacao family.
changes.quote: "The huge chocolate-mothballs-cucumber accord of Black Orchid was a clever idea"

note: The review is filed under the eau de toilette but describes the 2006 original's accord; the 'mothballs' facet fits the patchouli tags and the 'cucumber' facet has no clear family.
The Guide reviews only the Sauvage EDT and EDP; the Elixir postdates it.

guide_verdict: 2 stars, aromatic fougère: a pushy Cool Water imitation
note: The Guide's aromatic fougère label fits the lavender and woody-amber tags.

guide_verdict: 3 stars, citrus fougère: Cool Water and Light Blue clichés made refined
note: Both sources class it as a fougère (Scent and Chemistry lists 'Bleu' 2014 among fougères to study) yet no stage carries lavender, tonka or moss; not proposed because neither names those materials in it.

Scent and Chemistry reports 3% Operanide, a woody-mossy ambergris material, which fits the dominant woody_amber drydown.

guide_verdict: 1 star, fruity floral: a derivative linear clone

The Guide reviews only the original Stronger With You; this flanker is not a clone, so nothing was transferred.
